clue.text: Management game played by a lot of fans at length

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are toyed with and moved about, so the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team-management game enjoyed by huge numbers of supporters for hours at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of the game's players, but 'by a lot of fans at' rearranges, with L for 'length' added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Players act as virtual managers, picking squads of real footballers and scoring from their real matches.

clue.text: Enthused about job, I spread celebratory flyers with reports

indicators.note: the word for enthused goes around the word for job, so 'about' means wrapping round

parts.note: fired up, so enthused gives fired
work is a job
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled with a new job hands out leaflets about a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' look like leaflets, but here they are rockets, and 'reports' are their bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets that fly up and explode with bangs at a celebration make up a pyrotechnic show.

clue.text: Rings for righteous local protestor to come to hearing

indicators.note: a word that comes to hearing is one spoken aloud, so the protestor's name is heard

parts.note: a nimby (not in my back yard) objects to developments near home

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood campaigner is due to appear at a public inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a planning inquiry but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Haloes, the circles of light painted round saints' heads, are nimbuses, plural in Latin form.

clue.text: New Labour's no match for overpowering European dictator

indicators.note: overpowering is read as holding down and surrounding, so the shuffled letters enclose the European letter
new suggests making a new version, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is spelt out here, giving its S as a letter

explanation.surface: New Labour cannot compete with a dominant Continental tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Labour' reads as the political brand, but 'New' is the anagram signal on the fourteen letters, and 'overpowering' sets the European letter inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with unlimited power, answerable to nobody, is a dictator in all but title.

clue.text: Dated you, then married, in dark comedy

parts.note: ye is an old-fashioned form of you

indicators.note: the abbreviation for married goes in the word for dark

parts.note: sinister means dark or menacing

explanation.surface: A couple dated, then married, in a black comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like going out together but means old-fashioned. YES MINISTER is a classic British TV sitcom about a government minister and his civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated BBC sitcom of the 1980s satirising Whitehall, so an example of television comedy.

clue.text: To have present that's new becomes the ultimate!

indicators.note: the letter for new becomes the last one, so it shifts to the end of the word

parts.note: now means the present time

explanation.surface: Being given a brand-new gift makes a person feel on top of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to hold it as your property.

clue.text: All you need after bat, net and lines arranged on top of board?

definitions.text: All you need after bat, net and lines arranged on top of board?

indicators.note: the word All is placed after the rest
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of bat, net and lines are reshuffled
the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue

explanation.surface: Once you have a bat, a net and a marked-out table, only one more item is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: bat, net and a lined board are on hand, and what is still needed is the small ball.
explanation.definitionFit: After bat, net and a lined table top, the last piece of equipment for ping-pong is the small celluloid sphere.

clue.text: Short length of hose hurt, striking head with blow

indicators.note: striking out the head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to rankle is to hurt or cause lasting resentment
a sock is a punch or blow

explanation.surface: A hosepipe injury causes someone to hit their head on the way down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' looks like a garden pipe but means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose here means stockings, and a short sock reaching only to the joint above the foot is a brief one.

clue.text: Being collected from flat, boy and girl going by van

parts.note: level means flat
the van is the front or head
Ed is a boy's name
Ness is a girl's name, short for Vanessa or Agnes

explanation.surface: A couple are picked up from their apartment by a removal van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' looks like being picked up, but means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and composed means staying sensible under pressure, a quality of good judgement.

clue.text: African ruler once cut short holiday to arrest US spy

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the shortened word grips the spy's name
cut short means losing its final letter

parts.note: a rest is a holiday or break
Aldrich Ames was a CIA officer who spied for the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: A brief break is spoilt when police detain an American agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' leaves RES from REST, which then holds AMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Several ancient Egyptian pharaohs bore this name, so a ruler in Africa long ago.

clue.text: Writer shoved inside after arrest and fine

indicators.note: the middle letters come after the other two pieces

parts.note: to nab is to arrest
OK means fine

indicators.note: inside here means the central letters of the word shoved

explanation.surface: An author is thrown into a cell after being arrested and fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoved inside' looks like being jailed, but takes OV, the middle two letters of 'shoved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American author of Lolita.

clue.text: Snooker star's wife back to hold hands with one

indicators.note: to hold is to grip, so the word for back closes around the other letters

parts.note: hind means rear or back, as in hind legs
R and L stand for right and left, a pair of hands
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A snooker player's wife returns to hold hands with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like returning but is HIND. Jimmy White, a famous English snooker player, is nicknamed the Whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Jimmy White, a long-serving star of the green baize.

clue.text: Perception is research establishment people have stopped backing Irish politician

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these words sit inside the reversed politician
backing means running backwards, so the politician's letters are reversed

parts.note: TD stands for Teachta Dála, a member of the Irish parliament
CERN is the European particle-physics laboratory near Geneva
men are people

explanation.surface: A scientist senses that staff have blocked support for a Dublin legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: TD backwards is DT, which ISCERNMEN fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen judgement or insight is a form of perception.

clue.text: Energy source for Surrey town

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A power supply is being sought for a town in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: EWELL is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A town near Epsom in the county south-west of London.

clue.text: Share concession getting consent from Barker Bros?

definitions.meaning: an offer to existing shareholders to buy new shares at a discount
as if said aloud: brothers of the tennis star Sue Barker might agree with their sister by saying '...'

explanation.surface: A stock-market offer requires permission from a family firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Barker is a British tennis player turned BBC presenter; her imagined brothers would give consent with 'Right, sis Sue!', which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A company offers its existing stockholders new stock at a discount, a kind of corporate offer to members.

clue.text: Assume in sentiment solver's approving words

indicators.note: the word for assume goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: goo is sentimentality
you is the solver, the person addressed
to don is to put on or assume

explanation.surface: Someone praises the solver for taking a sentimental line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solver's' is YOU, with 's as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of congratulation or praise, so words that approve.

clue.text: Some reflecting moved one to find autumn work, perhaps

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the letters run backwards
some of these words gives a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person was moved to write about autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: EDO sits in 'moveD One' and reverses. Keats's To Autumn is a famous poem of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote a famous lyric poem to the season, so an example of this verse form.

clue.text: To be redeemed, last of all turning to God

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the picked letters are read backwards
the last letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A sinner finally turns to God for salvation.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters O, E, D reversed give DEO, the Latin for 'to God'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin dative form meaning for or towards the deity, familiar from Deo gratias.

clue.text: To Denmark he travels, out of habit

indicators.note: travels suggests moving about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun travels to Denmark, having left her order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like custom, but is clothing: out of it, one is stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entirely unclothed, as on the day of birth, is being out of any clothing.

clue.text: Neck that's not long broken by pressure

indicators.note: broken by means split open by a letter inserted

parts.note: soon means before long
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A neck that breaks quickly under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is a verb: to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle, an old-fashioned word for romantic canoodling.

clue.text: Grin insanely and bear place for an eternity?

indicators.note: insanely suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: to stand is to bear or tolerate

explanation.surface: Someone smiles madly and puts up with being somewhere forever.
explanation.walkthrough: An eternity ring is a band of stones, so 'an eternity' is a ring and its place is a stand for rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for keeping jewellery on, such as an eternity band.

clue.text: Midge got beneath street map for shade

indicators.note: in a down clue the musician sits beneath the map

parts.note: the A-Z is a London street atlas
Midge Ure is the Scottish singer of Ultravox

explanation.surface: An insect turned up under a street map in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midge' looks like an insect but is Midge Ure, the musician. The A-Z is a well-known British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright sky-blue colour, so a particular shade.

clue.text: Royal correspondent's boss going on set in films

indicators.note: the other two pieces go on after the first

parts.note: to lay is to set down
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
the editor, abbreviated ED, is the boss of a newspaper correspondent

explanation.surface: A palace reporter's editor is visiting a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'films' looks like cinema but means thin coatings.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in thin sheets one on top of another, like coats of a coating.

clue.text: Couple's forte somersaulting topless!

indicators.note: somersaulting means turning head over heels, so the letters run upwards
topless means the first letter is lost

parts.note: forte in music means loud

explanation.surface: A pair performing an acrobatic act without clothes on top.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUD loses its top to make OUD, which flips. 'forte' looks like a strength, but is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of performers is a twosome.

clue.text: English twins on holiday in Brussels one sent to the country?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means coming after, so the twins follow
in means placed inside, so the holiday word sits within the letters for Brussels

parts.note: Brussels, home of its institutions, stands for the EU
vac is short for vacation, a holiday
two copies of E, the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Two English siblings on holiday in Belgium are sent out to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Second World War British city children were sent to the countryside for safety; 'Brussels' stands for the EU, whose headquarters are there.
explanation.definitionFit: A child moved out of a city to rural safety in wartime was a refugee of this kind.

clue.text: Away-from-home crowd touring hard, people crying out for shelter?

definitions.text: Away-from-home crowd touring hard, people crying out for shelter?

indicators.note: to shelter something is to cover it, so the shouters enclose the rest

parts.note: yellers are people who shout

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the first pieces surround the letter for hard

parts.note: out means not at home
a host is a large crowd
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Travelling supporters on a hard tour shout for somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue pictures backpackers calling out for a bed for the night, so the definition is the entire clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Young travellers who stay in cheap dormitories while touring need a roof overnight.
